points.description: Classification defined as mapping input data to discrete labels/classes (categories).
Regression defined as mapping input data to a continuous function / continuous real-valued outputs.
Error in classification is the number of misclassifications (count of wrongly labelled samples).
Error in regression is the summed distance (e.g. sum of differences/absolute or squared) between true and predicted values.

rubric.notes: Each point needs an explicit, correct statement using the terms discrete/labels, continuous/real values, number of misclassifications, and summed distance between true and predicted values. Vague wording (e.g. 'classification sorts things', 'regression predicts numbers' without continuous) earns nothing for that point. A wrong statement, such as swapping the two, cancels that point. The difference must come through in the answer; the error points are required, not optional.
